Senses.PreferredTarget: monastic robe, bowl, and personal effects
Senses.Explanation: The material monastic robe, alms bowl, and, by extension, personal effects kept with them. The allowlisted corpus has 513 hits in 115 texts, including records in which the objects are thrown onto a rock, lifted, carried, guarded, inventoried, or burned with a person's other implements. Monastic regulations also name a ‘robe-and-bowl attendant’ (衣鉢侍者, 9 hits in 3 texts), who receives the seal in one installation procedure. In the Caoqi record, this attendant raises the robe associated with the object that could not be lifted at Dayu Ridge. These passages keep the material objects and their custodial office visible even where the same pair also marks succession.
Senses.Note: This first sense covers the material pair and its administrative extension to personal effects and the attendant responsible for them. It is separated from the succession-token sense because regulations can order the objects burned or placed in custody without describing succession.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the robe and bowl as evidence of lineage succession
Senses.Explanation: The same physical robe and bowl treated as passed evidence of lineage succession. The corpus records ‘transmit the robe and bowl’ (傳衣鉢, 31 hits in 26 texts), ‘entrust the robe and bowl’ (付衣鉢, 10 hits in 8 texts), and one exact occurrence of ‘robe and bowl transmitted in succession’ (衣鉢相傳). The Dayu Ridge account explicitly calls the robe ‘a token of trust.’ Yuansou Xingduan says that Huangmei's robe and bowl were entrusted to Lu, while Qining Wenyi asks which robe and bowl Lu actually transmitted. The question is recorded as a question rather than resolved here into an object different from the material robe and bowl.
Senses.Note: Historical succession does not make this sense specific to a named individual. The selected passages show the physical token, later transmission language, and a later challenge about what was transmitted. The seven required definition formulas were searched; no additional lexical self-definition was found.

Occurrences.Kwic: 爭似老盧無用處，却傳衣鉢振真風。大眾，且道那個是老盧傳底衣鉢？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Qining Wenyi section. Qining Wenyi is the exact speaker who asks which robe and bowl Huineng transmitted.
The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Yuansou Xingduan section. Yuansou Xingduan is the exact speaker who says that Huangmei's robe and bowl were entrusted to Lu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曹溪守衣鉢侍者，因僧到，乃提起衣曰：者是大庾嶺頭提不起底。僧曰：為什麼却在上座手裏？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Remarks on Old Cases of the Chan Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), Caoqi robe account. An unnamed robe-and-bowl attendant is the exact event actor who raises the robe and identifies it as the one that could not be lifted at Dayu Ridge. The line, expanded contexts through ±10,000 characters, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not name the attendant.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衣鉢僅為師弟古卓老宿所藏。卓翁又終，其衣鉢相傳於南明之手十有餘年。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈嚴統解惑編). Prose narration reports the possession and transmission of Feiyin Tongrong’s robe and bowl.

ActorAttribution.ReviewedBy: Codex lane-C second independent semantic repair
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The prose narrator reports that Feiyin Tongrong’s robe and bowl were kept by disciples and transmitted to Nanming for more than ten years; the named people are possessions’ holders, not utterers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 釋迦文於然燈佛以無法得受記。盧老於黃梅。以本來無物親付衣鉢。至於生死之際。才自擔荷。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), instruction to Storekeeper Juemin. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker who says that Huangmei personally entrusted the robe and bowl to Lu because there was originally no thing.
